seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the answer, and I've written it to `answer.txt`. All three seats reached the same output independently from hand traces of `program.stamp` against the spec. I didn't run the program in an interpreter. After the room concluded I left it.

The agreed answer is:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

seats.text:
The program's output is below. It is in `answer.txt`, and room rq1 concluded on this exact text with 3/3 agreeing.

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I got this by tracing `program.stamp` by hand against `spec.txt`; I did not run it in an interpreter. The other two seats reached the same answer independently, and the room's verification gate was satisfied with `verify/seat-3` and seat-1's `verify/answer`.

My own challenge, on the `101 7 7 7` segment (the `shadow` and `pair` calls), was recorded as unresolved. It says the segment holds after re-tracing. I have left the room.
